issues: src/screens/ReceiptEntryScreen.tsx does not display the required "Check these details" helper text next to pre‑filled fields after OCR, nor does it mark those fields as untouched until the user edits or confirms them, contrary to the task specification.

src/screens/ReceiptEntryScreen.tsx uses the OCR step even on the web platform; the spec requires the Scan button to be disabled (or show a tooltip) on web and not attempt to call recognizeReceiptText, but the current implementation still shows an enabled button that throws at runtime.

src/lib/categories.ts hideCategory does not enforce the rule that a category used by any receipt cannot be deleted – the test suite expects hideCategory to fail in that case, but the function currently always succeeds, potentially allowing hidden categories that are in use without error handling.

src/lib/backup.ts restoreBackup does not correctly restore custom categories when older backups without a categories key are loaded – the code writes the categories data directly without merging with defaults, which could lose defaults if they are missing from the backup. A merge with defaults is needed to satisfy the requirement that older backups still restore default categories.
feedback: The OCR parsing and category logic pass unit tests, but the UI and backup integration do not fully meet the task requirements. Update ReceiptEntryScreen to show helper text for pre‑filled fields and disable the Scan button on web (or provide the tooltip). Adjust hideCategory to reject hiding a category that is currently in use by receipts. Ensure restoreBackup merges restored categories with defaults so older backups remain functional. After fixing these issues, re‑run the acceptance tests and static validation.
